category: Measures of health status
front: The composite health measure that calculates the overall disease burden by combining years of life lost (YLL) and years lost to disability (YLD) is known as [___].
back: Disability-adjusted life years (DALY). It represents one year of healthy life lost. It captures the population impact of both fatal and non-fatal disabling conditions through a single measure.

category: Measures of health status
front: A health administrator evaluates a new treatment by multiplying the years of life gained by a utility factor (0.0 to 1.0) reflecting the patient's health quality. This assessment tool is the [___].
back: Quality-adjusted life years (QALY). It assesses value for money in medical interventions. A value of 1.0 represents one year of perfect health, while 0.0 represents death.

category: Measures of health status
front: Explain the rationale behind social weighting within the framework of Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs).
back: Social weighting assigns higher value to years lived as a young adult compared to children or the elderly. This reflects society's interest in economic productivity and return on investment in upbringing.

category: Measures of health status
front: Contrast the components of the Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) with standard mortality-only indicators.
back: PQLI consolidates three specific indicators: infant mortality, life expectancy at age one, and literacy. Unlike mortality rates alone, it provides a composite index reflecting the quality of life enjoyed by communities.

category: Measures of health status
front: Differentiate the primary focus of Disability-free life expectancy (DFLE) from general life expectancy statistics.
back: DFLE, or active life expectancy, calculates the average years an individual is expected to live free of disability. It prioritizes functional health and quality over the mere quantity of years lived.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: The single measure used to capture the population impact of both fatal and non-fatal disabling conditions, calculated as the sum of YLL and YLD, is the [___].
back:
• Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY)
• Formula: DALY = Years of Life Lost (YLL) + Years Lived with Disability (YLD)
• Represents one year of healthy life lost.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: A government health department evaluates a new chemotherapy regimen to see if the added survival years provide high 'utility' (perfect health = 1.0). Name the specific metric used for this cost-utility assessment.
back:
• Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
• Measures both quantity and quality of life lived
• Used to assess value for money of medical interventions.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Describe the mechanism of 'social weighting' applied in DALY calculations regarding different age groups.
back:
• Values years lived as a young adult more than childhood or old age
• Reflects societal interest in economic productivity
• Accounts for return on investment in a person's upbringing.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Contrast the standard reference used for measuring premature mortality in DALYs versus the utility scale used in QALYs.
back:
• DALY: Uses Japanese life expectancy as the global standard for premature death.
• QALY: Uses a utility scale where 1.0 is perfect health and 0.0 is death.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Explain why psychiatric conditions may have a high DALY despite having a low percentage of total deaths (YLL).
back:
• Psychiatric conditions cause high YLD (Years Lived with Disability)
• Account for ~28% of years lived with disability globally
• Impact is measured via time spent in suboptimal health rather than mortality.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: The composite index used to assess the quality of life in populations by consolidating infant mortality, life expectancy at age one, and literacy is the [___].
back: Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI). It integrates health indicators with educational status to provide a multidimensional profile of a population's wellbeing.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: A health commission evaluates the cost-effectiveness of a new dialysis protocol by multiplying the years of life added by a utility value ranging from 0 to 1. This assessment metric is known as [___].
back: Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALY). It measures both the quality and quantity of life lived to determine the value for money of medical interventions.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Explain the calculation and role of Years Lost to Disability (YLD) within the DALY framework.
back: YLD is calculated by multiplying incident cases of illness/injury by the average duration and a severity weighting factor (0 for health, 1 for death). It measures the non-fatal burden of chronic conditions.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Contrast the focus of Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY) with Disability-Free Life Expectancy (DFLE) in evaluating health status.
back: DALY measures total disease burden (years lost to premature death and disability). DFLE (active life expectancy) measures the positive average number of years an individual is expected to live without functional limitations.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Justify the use of 'social weighting' when calculating DALYs for a population's disease burden.
back: Social weighting values years lived as a young adult more highly than childhood or old age. This reflects societal interest in productivity and a return on investment for child upbringing.

category: Measures of health status
front: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is a composite measure that consolidates infant mortality, life expectancy at age one, and [___].
back:
• Literacy rate.
• Used to assess quality of life beyond economic growth.

category: Measures of health status
front: A patient survives a stroke but lives the next 10 years with a disability weighting of 0.5. State the number of Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY) contributed by these years of disability.
back:
• 5 DALYs.
• Calculated as Years Lost to Disability (YLD) = duration (10) × severity weighting (0.5).

category: Measures of health status
front: Explain the role of 'social weighting' in the calculation of Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs).
back:
• Assigns higher value to young adult years.
• Reflects societal interest in economic productivity and return on investment in upbringing.

category: Measures of health status
front: Contrast the utility of mortality rates versus Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) when evaluating the public health burden of psychiatric conditions.
back:
• Mortality: Very low impact (approx. 1.4% of deaths).
• DALYs: High impact (approx. 28% of years lived with disability).
• Highlights chronic morbidity over acute lethality.

category: Measures of health status
front: Identify the primary baseline population used as the standard for measuring premature death (YLL) in global health statistics.
back:
• Japanese life expectancy statistics.
• Chosen because they represent the longest life expectancy globally.

category: Measures of health status
front: The average number of years an individual is expected to live without functional limitations or mobility restrictions is known as [___].
back:
• Disability-free life expectancy (DFLE).
• Also called active life expectancy.

category: Measures of health status
front: A health department uses doctor-population ratios and bed-occupancy rates to assess a region. Categorize these specific health status indicators.
back:
• Health care delivery and utilization indicators.
• Measures availability and use of medical resources.

category: Measures of health status
front: Describe how the Human Development Index (HDI) differs from traditional mortality-based indicators in assessing a nation's health.
back:
• HDI is multidimensional.
• Incorporates health (life expectancy), knowledge (literacy), and standard of living (GNP).

category: Measures of health status
front: Distinguish between the calculation components of YLL and YLD within the DALY framework.
back:
• YLL: Number of deaths × expected remaining years of life.
• YLD: Incident cases × duration × severity weighting.

category: Measures of health status
front: List the three categories of indicators used to assess the socio-environmental health status of a community.
back:
• Suicide rates (Social/Mental).
• Pollution levels.
• Access to safe water and sanitation.

category: Life expectancy
front: The average number of years an individual is expected to live free of functional limitations or impairments if current trends continue is termed [___].
back:
* Disability-free life expectancy (DFLE).
* Also known as Active Life Expectancy.
* Reflects the quantity of life lived without disability.

category: Life expectancy
front: A health board evaluates a treatment that adds 4 years to a patient's life, but with a utility value of 0.5 due to side effects. Calculate the Quality-adjusted life years (QALYs).
back:
* 2 QALYs (4 years x 0.5 utility value).
* QALY measures both quality and quantity of life.
* Used to assess value for money in medical interventions.

category: Life expectancy
front: Explain how the Disability-adjusted life years (DALY) formula integrates both fatal and non-fatal health outcomes.
back:
* DALY = YLL + YLD.
* YLL (Years of Lost Life): Captures premature mortality.
* YLD (Years Lost to Disability): Captures the impact of living with illness.

category: Life expectancy
front: Contrast the significance of a single unit of DALY versus a single unit of QALY in health economics.
back:
* 1 DALY: Represents one year of healthy life lost (measure of burden).
* 1 QALY: Represents one year of life lived in perfect health (measure of benefit).

category: Life expectancy
front: Name the three specific indicators consolidated to calculate the Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI).
back:
* Infant mortality.
* Life expectancy at age one.
* Literacy rate.
* It measures quality of life rather than just economic growth.

category: Life expectancy
front: In the calculation of DALYs, the international standard for measuring premature death is based on the life expectancy of [___].
back:
* Japanese population.
* Japan is used as the standard because it has the longest global life expectancy.

category: Life expectancy
front: A population study shows that neuropsychiatric disorders account for 28% of disability but only 1% of deaths. Determine the impact of these conditions on DALYs.
back:
* They have a massive impact on DALYs.
* Primarily increase YLD (Years Lost to Disability).
* Demonstrate that mortality alone is a poor indicator of disease burden.

category: Life expectancy
front: Describe the rationale for 'social weighting' in DALY calculations regarding different age groups.
back:
* Values years lived as a young adult more highly than childhood or old age.
* Reflects societal interest in economic productivity.
* Considers the return on investment in upbringing.

category: Life expectancy
front: Contrast the 'Years of Lost Life' (YLL) calculation with the 'Years Lost to Disability' (YLD) calculation.
back:
* YLL: Number of deaths multiplied by standard life expectancy at age of death.
* YLD: Incident cases multiplied by duration and a severity weighting factor (0 to 1).

category: Life expectancy
front: Identify the primary limitation of using simple life expectancy as the sole indicator of a nation's health status.
back:
* It only measures the quantity of years.
* It fails to account for the quality of life or the burden of non-fatal disabilities.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is a composite index consolidating three specific indicators: infant mortality, life expectancy at age one, and [___].
back: Literacy. Unlike purely economic measures like GNP, PQLI focuses on social well-being and basic human needs to assess the quality of life within a population.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: A patient with terminal cancer receives palliative care that extends life by 2 years with a utility value of 0.4. Calculate the Quality-adjusted life years (QALY) for this patient.
back: 0.8 QALY. Calculation: 2 years × 0.4 utility value. QALY is a measure of disease burden that assesses the value of medical interventions by combining quality and quantity of life.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Explain how the Disability-adjusted life years (DALY) formula integrates both fatal and non-fatal disease outcomes into a single metric.
back: DALY = YLL + YLD. It sums Years of Lost Life (YLL) due to premature death and Years Lost to Disability (YLD) from incident cases of illness or injury.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Contrast the utility of Disability-free life expectancy (DFLE) with that of traditional life expectancy in geriatric health assessment.
back: Life expectancy measures total years lived. DFLE (active life expectancy) measures only the years lived without functional limitations or disability, reflecting a higher quality of life.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Identify the standard population used for measuring premature death in DALY calculations and justify its selection.
back: Japanese life expectancy. It is used as the global standard for premature mortality because the Japanese population holds the record for the longest life expectancy.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: The social weighting system in DALY calculations values years lived as a [___] more highly than those of young children or the elderly.
back: Young adult. This reflects society's interest in economic productivity and gaining a return on the investment made during a person's upbringing.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: A health report indicates that psychiatric conditions account for 28% of YLD but only 1.1% of YLL. Interpret what this means for the population's health focus.
back: It indicates a high morbidity burden. While psychiatric conditions rarely cause premature death, they significantly degrade the quality of life, contributing heavily to the total DALYs.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Describe the calculation of Years Lost to Disability (YLD) and the significance of the weighting factor used.
back: YLD = Incident cases × duration × severity weight. The weight ranges from 0 (perfect health) to 1 (death), quantifying the specific impact of a disease on functioning.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Distinguish between the purpose of measuring 'health care delivery' versus 'health care utilization' as indicators of health status.
back: Delivery (e.g., doctor-population ratio) measures available resources. Utilization (e.g., immunization coverage, bed-occupancy) measures how effectively the population actually accesses and uses those resources.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Define one 'Quality-adjusted life year' (QALY) in terms of life duration and health status.
back: One QALY equals one year of life lived in perfect health (1 year × 1.0 utility). It is the gold standard for assessing 'value for money' in medical interventions.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: One [___] represents the loss of one year of healthy life due to premature death or disability.
back:
Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY). 
- It combines mortality and morbidity into one unit.
- DALY = YLL (Years of Lost Life) + YLD (Years Lost to Disability).

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: A psychiatric patient has a condition with a very low mortality rate but high chronic morbidity. Identify the indicator that best captures this specific disease burden.
back:
Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY). 
- Psychiatric conditions account for 28% of YLD (Years Lived with Disability).
- It highlights non-fatal but highly disabling conditions.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Explain how Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALY) are used to determine the value of a medical intervention.
back:
QALY integrates quantity and quality of life.
- One year in perfect health = 1.0 QALY.
- It helps assess 'value for money' by calculating extra years of healthy life added by treatment.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Contrast the focus of Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALY) versus Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY).
back:
QALY measures health gain (benefit-oriented).
- DALY measures disease burden (loss-oriented).
- QALY is used for economic evaluation; DALY is used for global burden of disease assessment.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Justify why 'social weighting' in DALY calculations assigns higher value to years lived as a young adult.
back:
Reflects societal interest in economic productivity.
- Prioritizes individuals who provide a return on investment for upbringing.
- Recognizes the higher social and economic roles of adults over children or elderly.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is a composite measure including infant mortality, literacy, and [___].
back:
Life expectancy at age one.
- It differs from the Human Development Index (HDI).
- It assesses the physical well-being of a population.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: A public health study tracks the 'active life expectancy' of a population to see how many years people live without restricted mobility. Name this indicator.
back:
Disability-Free Life Expectancy (DFLE).
- It measures the average years expected to be lived free of disability.
- Also known as active life expectancy.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Detail the methodology used to calculate Years of Lost Life (YLL) in the DALY framework.
back:
Number of deaths at each age multiplied by the expected remaining years of life.
- It uses a global standard life expectancy.
- Japanese life expectancy is typically used as the benchmark.

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: Distinguish between mortality and morbidity indicators in the context of health status measurement.
back:
Mortality: Relates to death data (e.g., life expectancy, infant mortality).
- Morbidity: Relates to illness and sickness (e.g., incidence, prevalence, notification rates).

category: Discuss the significance of quality of life in disease and treatment settings
front: List the primary purposes for measuring health status in a community beyond simple mortality tracking.
back:
Assess care needs.
- Allocate health resources.
- Compare populations.
- Evaluate the effectiveness of health programs.

category: Measures of health status
front: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is a composite index consolidating three indicators: infant mortality, life expectancy at age one, and [___].
back:
• Literacy rate
• Consolidates social/demographic data
• Measures quality of life beyond simple mortality

category: Measures of health status
front: A public health survey reveals that psychiatric conditions contribute to 28% of years lived with disability but very few deaths. The specific health status measure that best captures this overall disease burden is [___].
back:
• Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY)
• Sums YLL (Years of Life Lost) and YLD (Years Lost to Disability)
• One DALY equals one year of healthy life lost

category: Measures of health status
front: Explain the integration of quality and quantity of life within the Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY) calculation for medical interventions.
back:
• Calculated as years of life added multiplied by a utility value
• Utility value ranges from 1.0 (perfect health) to 0.0 (death)
• Used to assess value for money in healthcare

category: Measures of health status
front: A researcher is comparing populations where one group has high longevity with chronic illness and another has shorter, healthier lifespans. Contrast the utility of Disability-free life expectancy (DFLE) versus DALY.
back:
• DFLE: Average years lived without disability
• DALY: Total gap between current health and ideal health
• DALY measures burden; DFLE measures expectation

category: Measures of health status
front: Detail the concept of 'social weighting' as applied to the calculation of Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs).
back:
• Assigns higher value to years lived as a young adult
• Reflects societal interest in economic productivity
• Prioritizes return on investment in child upbringing

category: Measures of health status
front: The [___] rate is a basic mortality indicator that provides the total number of deaths per 1,000 population in a year, though it does not account for age structure.
back:
• Crude Death Rate
• Primary mortality indicator
• Used for general population health comparisons

category: Measures of health status
front: A health officer tracks bed-occupancy rates and doctor-population ratios to assess a district's status. Categorize these specific indicators.
back:
• Health care delivery and utilization indicators
• Reflects availability and use of medical resources
• Measures equity and accessibility of care

category: Measures of health status
front: Describe the two distinct mathematical components that are summed to calculate the total Disability-adjusted life years (DALY) for a chronic condition.
back:
• Years of Lost Life (YLL): Deaths multiplied by standard life expectancy
• Years Lost to Disability (YLD): Incident cases multiplied by duration and severity weighting

category: Measures of health status
front: Distinguish between incidence and prevalence as morbidity indicators used in health status measurement.
back:
• Incidence: Number of new cases in a specific period
• Prevalence: Total number of existing cases (new and old)
• Incidence reflects risk; prevalence reflects burden

category: Measures of health status
front: Identify the national population whose life expectancy is used as the global standard for calculating Years of Life Lost (YLL) in DALY studies.
back:
• Japanese population
• Chosen for having the longest global life expectancy
• Serves as the benchmark for premature death

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: The single health measure that combines the impact of premature mortality (YLL) and the impact of non-fatal disabling conditions (YLD) is [___].
back:
Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY).
- 1 DALY = 1 year of healthy life lost.
- It measures the gap between current health and an ideal health state.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: A public health survey finds that while Major Depressive Disorder has low mortality, it causes significant long-term functional impairment. Identify the metric that best captures this burden.
back:
Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY).
- Specifically the YLD (Years Lost to Disability) component.
- Captures the massive impact of non-fatal psychiatric conditions on population health.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Explain the role of the 'utility value' in the calculation of Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALY).
back:
Utility values weight the quality of life from 0.0 (death) to 1.0 (perfect health).
- Formula: Years of life × Utility value = QALY.
- Used to assess 'value for money' in interventions.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Contrast the fundamental focus of QALY with that of DALY regarding health outcomes.
back:
- QALY: Focuses on health GAINS (years of life added by an intervention).
- DALY: Focuses on health LOSS (burden of disease or premature death).

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Explain the rationale behind 'social weighting' used in the global burden of disease studies.
back:
Social weighting assigns higher value to years lived as a young adult.
- Reflects societal interest in productivity.
- Values the return on investment in a person's upbringing.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is a composite index consolidating three indicators: infant mortality, literacy, and [___].
back:
Life expectancy at age one.
- It excludes economic indicators like GNP.
- Measures purely social and physical quality of life.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: A 60-year-old patient receives a surgical intervention that improves their health state from a utility of 0.5 to 0.8 for the next 10 years. Calculate the QALYs gained.
back:
3.0 QALYs.
- Calculation: (0.8 - 0.5) × 10 years = 3.0.
- Quantifies the improvement in quality and quantity of life.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Detail how the 'Years Lost to Disability' (YLD) component of a DALY is derived.
back:
YLD = Incident cases × Average duration × Disability weight.
- Weights range from 0 (perfect health) to 1 (death).
- Represents the non-fatal component of disease burden.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Distinguish Disability-Free Life Expectancy (DFLE) from the DALY measure.
back:
- DFLE: The average years an individual is expected to live WITHOUT disability.
- DALY: The total years LOST due to disability or early death.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Identify the specific population standard used to calculate 'Years of Lost Life' (YLL) in the original DALY methodology.
back:
Japanese life expectancy statistics.
- Selected because the Japanese have the longest life expectancy globally.
- Used as the benchmark for measuring premature death.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: One DALY is equivalent to [___] year(s) of healthy life lost.
back:
• One year.
• It represents the gap between current health and an ideal health situation.
• Combines premature mortality (YLL) and morbidity (YLD).

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: A public health official is calculating the burden of a chronic non-fatal disease like major depression. Which specific component of the DALY formula accounts for the years spent in suboptimal health?
back:
• YLD (Years Lived with Disability).
• Calculation: Incident cases × average duration × disability weight.
• Accounts for the impact of non-fatal disabling conditions.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Explain the role of the "utility value" when determining Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALY) for a medical intervention.
back:
• It weights life years by health quality.
• Scale: 1.0 (perfect health) to 0.0 (death).
• QALY = Years of life added × Utility value.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
coreConcept: Inverse scaling of QALY vs DALY
front: Contrast the "0 to 1" scale used in QALYs versus the "0 to 1" weighting system used in the YLD component of DALYs.
back:
• QALY: 1.0 is Perfect Health; 0.0 is Death.
• DALY (YLD): 0.0 is Perfect Health; 1.0 is Death.
• They are inverse indicators of health status.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Identify the primary purpose of using QALYs in healthcare policy and resource allocation.
back:
• Assesses "value for money."
• Conducts cost-effectiveness analysis of medical interventions.
• Prioritizes treatments providing maximum quality years per unit cost.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: The DALY formula is expressed as DALY = [___] + [___].
back:
• YLL (Years of Life Lost).
• YLD (Years Lived with Disability).
• YLL measures premature death; YLD measures living with illness.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: A country implements "social weighting" in its DALY assessments. Explain why a year of life for a 25-year-old might be valued more than a year for an infant.
back:
• Reflects societal interest in economic productivity.
• Accounts for return on investment in child upbringing.
• Prioritizes the most economically active age groups.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Describe how the Global Burden of Disease project calculates the Years of Life Lost (YLL) component for a population.
back:
• Number of deaths at each age × standard remaining life expectancy.
• Uses Japanese life expectancy as the global standard.
• Quantifies the impact of premature mortality.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Contrast the Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) with the Human Development Index (HDI) based on their core indicators.
back:
• PQLI: Infant mortality, life expectancy (age 1), and literacy.
• HDI: Includes PQLI factors plus socioeconomic indicators (e.g., GNP/income).
• HDI is a broader measure of development.

category: Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY) and Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY)
front: Specify the country whose statistics serve as the "global standard" for life expectancy in DALY calculations.
back:
• Japan.
• Chosen due to having the longest global life expectancy.
• Used to define the maximum potential healthy life.

category: Life expectancy
coreConcept: Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) Components
front: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is a composite measure that consolidates three specific indicators: infant mortality, literacy, and [___].
back:
• Life expectancy at age one.
• Note: It is used as a composite index to measure the quality of life enjoyed by a community.

category: Life expectancy
front: A patient receives a surgical intervention that provides 4 additional years of life, but with a utility value of 0.5 due to residual morbidity. Calculate the total Quality-adjusted life years (QALY) gained.
back:
• 2 QALYs.
• Calculation: 4 years × 0.5 utility value = 2 QALYs.
• Represents 1 year of life lived in perfect health.

category: Life expectancy
front: Explain the mathematical components used to calculate Disability-adjusted life years (DALY) as a measure of the global burden of disease.
back:
• DALY = YLL + YLD.
• YLL: Years of lost life due to premature mortality.
• YLD: Years lost to disability (incident cases × duration × severity weight).

category: Life expectancy
coreConcept: Life Expectancy vs. Disability-Free Life Expectancy
front: Contrast the utility of Life Expectancy versus Disability-free life expectancy (DFLE) in assessing a population's healthcare needs.
back:
• Life Expectancy: Average total years lived (Mortality indicator).
• DFLE (Active Life Expectancy): Average years lived without limitations/disability.
• DFLE better reflects quality and 'active' health status.

category: Life expectancy
front: Identify the national population used as the global standard for measuring premature death in DALY calculations and the underlying justification.
back:
• Japanese population.
• Justification: They possess the longest life expectancy globally.
• Used to calculate the 'expected remaining years of life' standard.

category: Life expectancy
front: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is calculated using three indicators: infant mortality, literacy, and [___].
back: Life expectancy at age one. PQLI consolidates these three to provide a composite index of health and development beyond mere mortality rates.

category: Life expectancy
front: A health board evaluates a new chemotherapy regimen by calculating years of life added adjusted for patient-reported wellbeing. This metric is known as [___].
back: Quality-adjusted life years (QALY). It measures both the quality and quantity of life lived, where 1.0 represents a year of perfect health.

category: Life expectancy
front: Explain the method used to calculate Years Lost to Disability (YLD) within the DALY framework.
back: Multiply the number of incident cases by: 1. Average duration of the disease. 2. A severity weighting factor (0 for perfect health to 1 for death).

category: Life expectancy
front: Contrast Disability-adjusted life years (DALY) with Quality-adjusted life years (QALY) regarding their primary objective.
back: DALY measures total disease burden (years lost). QALY measures the value or benefit of a medical intervention (years gained in health).

category: Life expectancy
front: State the global standard used for measuring premature death in DALY calculations due to its high life expectancy.
back: Japanese life expectancy statistics. These are used as the benchmark because the Japanese population has the longest life expectancy globally.

category: Life expectancy
front: The formula for calculating Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALY) is [___].
back: YLL + YLD (Years of Lost Life + Years Lost to Disability). It captures the population impact of both fatal and non-fatal conditions.

category: Life expectancy
front: Psychiatric conditions often show low mortality but high years lived with disability. Which composite indicator best captures this specific public health burden?
back: Disability-adjusted life years (DALY). It reveals the massive impact of non-fatal disabling conditions that mortality data alone fails to capture.

category: Life expectancy
front: Describe how 'social weighting' influences the valuation of life years in health impact assessments.
back: It assigns higher value to years lived as a young adult compared to children or older adults. This reflects societal interest in economic productivity.

category: Life expectancy
front: Distinguish between Life Expectancy and Disability-free Life Expectancy (DFLE).
back: Life Expectancy: Average years an individual is expected to live. DFLE: Average years an individual lives free of disability given current mortality/disability patterns.

category: Life expectancy
front: Define the specific meaning of 'one DALY' in public health impact assessments.
back: One DALY is equal to one year of healthy life lost. It represents the gap between current health status and an ideal health situation.
